summaries.demographer: Miranda Johnson is a 40-year-old Black/African-American woman living alone in an owned townhouse in Strongsville, Ohio, with no spouse, cohabiting partner, or children (Q05, Q11, Q84, Q89). She was born in Cleveland and raised in the Cleveland area by both parents with one older brother in a stable, education-oriented household (Q87-Q99). She has a bachelor's degree and works full time as an operations supervisor, placing her in a stable single-income professional household with employer benefits and moderate assets such as homeownership and retirement savings (Q65, Q72, Q76, Q83). Her life course is strongly shaped by family, church, Great Migration heritage, and upward mobility through education and administrative leadership (Q01, Q47, Q108).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Miranda shows high planning orientation, future focus, and risk management through spreadsheet budgeting, automatic savings, certification study, and emergency funds (Q57, Q61, Q62, Q82). She responds to uncertainty by creating routines, lists, sinking funds, and documented workflows, both at home and work (Q15, Q50, Q65). Her choices are identity-linked: she invests time in church, mentoring, Black professional advancement, and youth coaching because these reinforce community obligations and self-concept (Q04, Q17, Q29, Q108). She is cautious but not deprived; she spends on fitness, food, family, and travel while cutting discretionary purchases when expenses rise (Q56-Q60).
summaries.political_scientist: Miranda is a fairly strong Democrat with center-left, pragmatic views focused on civil rights, voting access, public education, health care, workplace equity, and competent implementation (Q23-Q25, Q95-Q96). She votes regularly, researches candidates, and pays increasing attention to local institutions such as school boards, judges, and city government (Q23, Q25). Her politics are rooted in racial identity, church community, family history, and direct workplace experience with representation and accountability (Q26-Q30). She has participated in peaceful protest, donated to community causes, supported voter registration, and organized workplace equity conversations, indicating high civic engagement but not full-time campaign activism (Q23, Q29, Q47).
summaries.psychologist: Miranda presents as conscientious, socially vibrant, achievement-oriented, and emotionally self-aware, with a strong need for order, excellence, and meaningful contribution (Q01, Q02, Q65, Q109). She copes with stress through exercise, prayer, social support, scheduling, cooking, and occasional journaling, while recognizing tendencies toward over-responsibility and anxious rumination (Q43-Q45, Q50). Her self-concept combines warmth and discipline: she wants to be dependable, prepared, honest, and in people's corner, but she is learning boundaries (Q43, Q50, Q109). Family, faith, Black womanhood, and professional competence are central to her identity and motivation (Q01, Q28, Q47, Q108).
